0039203dc5.q: What is the Janus Plan framework and how does it help address high achiever burnout?
0039203dc5.a: The Janus Plan uses reflection on the past and intention toward the future as a threshold for change. It involves three core questions: what is really working well and worth keeping, what can you lay down that no longer serves you, and what is the real lesson you need to learn. By identifying a one-word theme for the new chapter, you can develop specific goals in support of that theme while acknowledging the good, bad, and ugly aspects of your past before moving forward.

328c96647b.q: What happened to Jobert Abueva on September 6, 1997 that became his turning point for recognizing burnout?
328c96647b.a: On September 6, 1997 in Hong Kong, after a long week of budget meetings and entertaining, Abueva woke up with a splitting headache, feeling numb and inebriated, unable to eat or get out of bed while watching Princess Diana's funeral coverage on BBC. This moment of complete physical and emotional collapse became his wake-up call that the relentless pace and constant work he had been sustaining was unsustainable, marking the genesis of his thinking about burnout, resilience, and recovery.

aced2060fc.q: How did Jobert Abueva use empirical self-observation to recognize and address the beliefs driving his burnout?
aced2060fc.a: During his recovery period, Abueva conducted an audit of his actual behaviors by tracking metrics: he found he was averaging only four to five hours of sleep per night instead of the eight-hour norm, and he marked on a calendar when anxiety and panic attacks occurred. This data-driven approach helped him identify the underlying beliefs fueling his burnout—such as 'rest is for the weak' and 'ambition at all costs'—which he then consciously rejected and replaced with healthier mindsets.

7250db97f8.q: What did Jobert Abueva do on his radical sabbatical after quitting his corporate job to recover from burnout?
7250db97f8.a: After leaving his marketing position, Abueva took a radical sabbatical to rediscover who he really was and how he wanted to show up in the world. He returned to the United States and took writing classes at the New School and the Gotham Writers Workshop in New York City to reconnect with his passion for writing that he had suppressed during his corporate career. He also moved out to the country for a period to get away from the chaos, spending several years writing before eventually re-entering the corporate space in a different sector.

271f45d8c5.q: What three reflection questions does the Janus Plan use to help people clarify what they really want?
271f45d8c5.a: The Janus Plan asks three core questions, whether at year-end, facing a specific challenge, or entering a new life stage: first, what is really working well and worth keeping as fuel for momentum; second, what can you lay down or let go of that no longer serves you and lightens your burden; and third, what is the real lesson you are trying to learn, which creates a mindset and framing shift that allows you to look forward like Janus toward the future.
